canonical_record.label: WHO sixth-edition semen examination and processing procedures
canonical_record.summary: The WHO sixth-edition semen manual describes procedures and methods for laboratory examination and processing of human semen.

sources.title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th ed

statement: The WHO sixth-edition semen manual describes procedures and methods for laboratory examination and processing of human semen.

scope.population: Human semen examined or processed in laboratory settings.
scope.assumptions: Description of the WHO sixth-edition manual, not an independently measured clinical outcome.
scope.uncertainty: The captured publication page establishes the manual's stated scope, not the validation of every individual protocol.

support.quote: The sixth edition of the WHO Manual for the Laboratory Examination and Processing of Human Semen is a reference document for procedures and methods for the laboratory examination and processing of human semen, which are intended to maintain and sustain

canonical_record.label: WHO-described clinical and research uses of semen analysis
canonical_record.summary: The WHO semen manual states that semen analysis may be useful for investigating male fertility status and monitoring spermatogenesis during and following male fertility regulation and other interventions, in clinical and research settings.

sources.title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th ed

statement: The WHO semen manual states that semen analysis may be useful for investigating male fertility status and monitoring spermatogenesis during and following male fertility regulation and other interventions, in clinical and research settings.

scope.population: Clinical and research examination of human semen in the contexts described by WHO.
scope.time: During and following male fertility regulation and other interventions, where monitoring is undertaken.
scope.assumptions: The source says semen analysis may be useful, not that it independently determines fertility in every individual.
scope.uncertainty: Utility is presented as a possible application rather than a guaranteed diagnostic or predictive result.

support.quote: Semen analysis may be useful in both clinical and research settings, for investigating male fertility status as well as monitoring spermatogenesis during and following male fertility regulation and other interventions.

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM varicocelectomy recommendation for selected infertile men
canonical_record.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends considering surgical varicocelectomy for men attempting conception who have palpable varicoceles, infertility and abnormal semen parameters, except azoospermic men; it labels this a moderate recommendation supported by Grade B evidence.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends considering surgical varicocelectomy for men attempting conception who have palpable varicoceles, infertility and abnormal semen parameters, except azoospermic men; it labels this a moderate recommendation supported by Grade B evidence.

scope.population: Men attempting to conceive with palpable varicoceles, infertility and abnormal semen parameters, excluding azoospermic men.
scope.assumptions: A guideline recommendation for consideration of surgery under the stated selection criteria.
scope.uncertainty: Moderate recommendation; Evidence Level Grade B. Does not guarantee improved fertility or apply to nonpalpable varicoceles or azoospermic men.

support.quote: Surgical varicocelectomy should be considered in men attempting to conceive, who have palpable varicocele(s), infertility, and abnormal semen parameters, except for azoospermic men.(Moderate Recommendation; Evidence Level: Grade B)

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM microdissection sperm retrieval recommendation in NOA
canonical_record.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends microdissection testicular sperm extraction for men with non-obstructive azoospermia undergoing sperm retrieval, assigning a moderate recommendation with Grade C evidence.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: The AUA/ASRM guideline recommends microdissection testicular sperm extraction for men with non-obstructive azoospermia undergoing sperm retrieval, assigning a moderate recommendation with Grade C evidence.

scope.population: Men with non-obstructive azoospermia undergoing sperm retrieval.
scope.assumptions: Procedure selection within the AUA/ASRM male-infertility guideline.
scope.uncertainty: Moderate recommendation; Evidence Level Grade C. This is not a guarantee of successful sperm retrieval.

support.quote: For men with NOA undergoing sperm retrieval, microdissection testicular sperm extraction (TESE) should be performed. (Moderate Recommendation; Evidence Level: Grade C)

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM recommendation against testosterone monotherapy when fertility is desired
canonical_record.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline states that testosterone monotherapy should not be prescribed to a male interested in current or future fertility, identifying this recommendation as a clinical principle.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: The AUA/ASRM guideline states that testosterone monotherapy should not be prescribed to a male interested in current or future fertility, identifying this recommendation as a clinical principle.

scope.population: Males interested in current or future fertility.
scope.time: Current or future reproductive intentions as specified by the guideline.
scope.assumptions: Refers specifically to testosterone monotherapy, not every possible treatment for low testosterone.
scope.uncertainty: Classified as a Clinical Principle by the guideline, not as a quantified randomized treatment effect.

support.quote: For the male interested in current or future fertility, testosterone monotherapy should not be prescribed. (Clinical Principle)

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM uncertainty regarding fertility supplements
canonical_record.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline reports that clear, reliable evidence is lacking for supplements offered to men attempting conception and describes their value for improving fertility outcomes as questionable.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: The AUA/ASRM guideline reports that clear, reliable evidence is lacking for supplements offered to men attempting conception and describes their value for improving fertility outcomes as questionable.

scope.population: Men attempting conception who are offered vitamins, antioxidants or nutritional supplement formulations.
scope.time: Evidence assessment in the retained guideline; no claim about subsequent trials.
scope.assumptions: The assessment concerns improving male fertility outcomes with the supplements described.
scope.uncertainty: Absence of clear reliable supportive evidence is not proof that every supplement is ineffective or harmful.

support.quote: There are no clear, reliable data to support use of the variety of supplements (vitamins, antioxidants, nutritional supplement formulations) that have been offered to men attempting conception. Current data suggest that they are likely not harmful, but they are of questionable value in improving fertility outcomes.

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM sperm banking recommendation before gonadotoxic therapy
canonical_record.summary: The AUA/ASRM guideline advises clinicians to encourage sperm banking, preferably multiple specimens when possible, before gonadotoxic therapy or other cancer treatment that may affect male fertility; it classifies this as expert opinion.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: The AUA/ASRM guideline advises clinicians to encourage sperm banking, preferably multiple specimens when possible, before gonadotoxic therapy or other cancer treatment that may affect male fertility; it classifies this as expert opinion.

scope.population: Men facing gonadotoxic therapy or other cancer treatment that may affect fertility.
scope.time: Before commencement of the relevant treatment.
scope.assumptions: Multiple specimens are preferred when possible, not represented as universally feasible or necessary.
scope.uncertainty: Expert Opinion classification; no guaranteed future fertility outcome is asserted.

support.quote: Clinicians should encourage men to bank sperm, preferably multiple specimens when possible, prior to commencement of gonadotoxic therapy or other cancer treatment that may affect fertility in men. (Expert Opinion)

canonical_record.label: AUA/ASRM-reported gaps in understanding male infertility causes
canonical_record.summary: In its future-directions discussion, the AUA/ASRM guideline states that the causes of male infertility, including their genetic basis, had been only superficially explained at the time of the guideline.

sources.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Infertility in Men: AUA/ASRM Guideline Part II

statement: In its future-directions discussion, the AUA/ASRM guideline states that the causes of male infertility, including their genetic basis, had been only superficially explained at the time of the guideline.

scope.population: The causes of male infertility, including genetic explanations, as discussed by the guideline authors.
scope.time: At the time of the retained guideline's assessment.
scope.assumptions: Historical statement of the authors' research assessment, not a claim that no causes were known or that the same gap remains unchanged today.
scope.uncertainty: The source gives a qualitative assessment, not a quantified fraction of unexplained cases.

support.quote: The causes of male infertility, including their genetic basis, have only been superficially explained at this time.

canonical_record.label: Endocrine Society hypogonadism diagnostic criteria
canonical_record.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends diagnosing hypogonadism only in men with compatible symptoms and signs and unequivocally and consistently low serum testosterone concentrations.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

statement: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends diagnosing hypogonadism only in men with compatible symptoms and signs and unequivocally and consistently low serum testosterone concentrations.

scope.population: Men evaluated for testosterone deficiency and hypogonadism.
scope.assumptions: The diagnosis requires both the stated clinical findings and the stated biochemical findings under the guideline.
scope.uncertainty: This is a guideline criterion, not evidence that one symptom or one low measurement is independently sufficient.
scope.quantifiers: Symptoms and signs together with unequivocally and consistently low serum testosterone.

support.quote: Recommends making a diagnosis of hypogonadism  only in men with symptoms and signs consistent with testosterone (T) deficiency  and unequivocally and consistently low serum T concentrations.

canonical_record.label: Endocrine Society recommendation for repeat morning testosterone measurement
canonical_record.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends confirming hypogonadism by repeating measurement of morning fasting total testosterone concentrations.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

statement: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends confirming hypogonadism by repeating measurement of morning fasting total testosterone concentrations.

scope.population: Men undergoing diagnostic confirmation of hypogonadism.
scope.time: Morning fasting measurement, repeated for confirmation.
scope.assumptions: Refers to diagnostic confirmation, not routine hormone monitoring of the general population.
scope.uncertainty: A recommended diagnostic procedure, not a guarantee that a repeated value establishes the diagnosis in isolation.
scope.quantifiers: Repeat the morning fasting total testosterone measurement.

support.quote: Recommend confirming the diagnosis by  repeating the measurement of morning fasting total T concentrations.

canonical_record.label: Endocrine Society hormonal evaluation of primary versus secondary hypogonadism
canonical_record.summary: For men with hypogonadism, the Endocrine Society guideline recommends measuring serum luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone concentrations to distinguish primary testicular from secondary pituitary-hypothalamic hypogonadism.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

statement: For men with hypogonadism, the Endocrine Society guideline recommends measuring serum luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone concentrations to distinguish primary testicular from secondary pituitary-hypothalamic hypogonadism.

scope.population: Men with hypogonadism undergoing evaluation of its origin.
scope.assumptions: Distinguishes primary testicular dysfunction from secondary pituitary-hypothalamic dysfunction using the specified serum hormones.
scope.uncertainty: The recommendation concerns diagnostic differentiation; it does not state that those measurements alone determine every underlying etiology.

support.quote: In men who have hypogonadism, we recommend distinguishing between primary (testicular) and secondary (pituitary–hypothalamic) hypogonadism by measuring serum luteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone concentrations.

canonical_record.label: Endocrine Society recommendation against routine population screening for hypogonadism
canonical_record.summary: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends against routine screening of men in the general population for hypogonadism.

sources.title: Testosterone Therapy for Hypogonadism Guideline Resources

statement: The Endocrine Society guideline recommends against routine screening of men in the general population for hypogonadism.

scope.population: Men in the general population, as distinguished from patients undergoing clinically indicated evaluation.
scope.assumptions: The restriction concerns routine population screening, not all testing for suspected hypogonadism.
scope.uncertainty: This is the cited guideline's recommendation and does not establish that diagnostic testing is inappropriate for symptomatic patients.
scope.quantifiers: Routine screening of the general male population.

support.quote: We recommend against routine screening of men in the general population for hypogonadism.
